title: Offline reinforcement learning identifies an AgBiI4 film-processing condition
summary: The Daisy framework combines SEM-image interpretation with offline reinforcement learning trained on historical Ag-Bi-I thin-film conditions and microstructure measurements. For AgBiI4, the planner proposed a condition outside the recorded combinations, and a newly fabricated film showed no visible pinholes and mean grain size 14.5% above the historical mean for defect-free samples. Its grain distribution was comparable to the best historical sample, so the study does not show that the new condition outperformed the previous best or improved device performance.
ai_technology: Daisy image-analysis models and offline reinforcement-learning synthesis planner trained on historical microstructure data

evidence.tested: A newly fabricated AgBiI4 film under the RL-proposed processing condition showed 0% visible defect coverage and mean grain size 14.5% above the historical mean for defect-free samples; its grain distribution was comparable to the best historical sample.
evidence.unknown: This is a thin-film morphology result; the new condition did not outperform the best historical sample and device-level optoelectronic performance was not established.
evidence.ai_role: Daisy uses ML models to interpret SEM morphology and an offline reinforcement-learning planner trained on historical synthesis conditions to propose a processing condition that was then fabricated and measured.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text as indexed, including article date, methods, results, author contributions and affiliations.
